hypothesis: A fixed EMA over sampled-PPO actor-head updates filters trajectory jitter and yields a stronger frozen greedy policy than the raw terminal actor without changing learned-policy inputs or rules.
material_change: Add checkpointed actor-head EMA instrumentation; train one 131072-physical-hand all-policy-heads trajectory and compare source, raw terminal, and EMA terminal on common-deck five-anchor evaluation.
baseline: Raw terminal actor from the identical training trajectory; legacy Standard10 greedy fresh20k -11.4275 bb/100 CI [-28.7124,5.8574], strict sampled -48.9778; prior imitation-teacher fresh20k about -18.5025.

result.summary: One 132553-physical-hand sampled PPO trajectory produced raw and decay-0.9 EMA actor endpoints; 61440 common-deck five-anchor hands compared source/raw/EMA, and independent raw-pair review passed.
result.conclusion: EMA preserved more of the source but underperformed the identical trajectory's raw terminal actor by 20.083 bb/100; only 1/5 anchor contrasts was positive. The EMA-source gain shows learning beat the source internally, not that averaging helped. Historical greedy-vs-sampled evidence therefore does not justify this fixed EMA mechanism, and the negative imitation-teacher evidence remains unreversed.
result.next_step: Retain the stronger frozen raw terminal endpoint as a candidate and run a small fresh Slumbot transfer gate before spending more training compute; do not expand EMA or imitation. If transfer is not competitive, diagnose the greedy/sampled contract with on-policy evaluation rather than another smoothing variant.
